To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a method for efficiently extracting information from neural spike trains recorded over time, which is based on non-negative factorization of a large space-by-time tensor, and we demonstrated that our approach is more robust than the standard non-negative factorization when baseline activity is present in the recorded data.
baseline-corrected space-time non-negative matrix decomposition of single-trial neural data improves stimulus decoding performance.
we developed a method to factorize single-trial spike trains into low-dimensional representations that capture efficiently both their spatial information and their temporal information.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing and evaluating new analytical methods for extracting low-dimensional information-rich representations from neural population activity.
finding efficient representations of neural activity that are useful in a variety of applications, from decoding to modeling.
the problem of how to efficiently represent and analyze neural activity recorded from multiple neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

baseline-corrected space by time non-negative matrix factorisation (STNMF) can be used to efficiently discount prestimulus baseline activity, and that in situations where the stimulus elicits strong change in firing rates, this can boost stimulus decoding performance.
the method presented in the article is a significant advance on previous methods.
our baseline-corrected space-time non-negative matrix decomposition is useful for finding a compact low-dimensional information-rich representation of single trial population spike train activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we developed a method to compactly represent the information that populations of neurons carry in their spatiotemporal activity, and we demonstrated its benefits on decoding the information that the retina encodes in its population activity.
our baseline-corrected tensor factorization can be useful in situations where the baseline activity is large and the stimulus evokes a strong change in the firing rate.
we developed a method to compactly represent the spatial and temporal dimensions of population spike trains and showed that taking the pre-stimulus activity into account can be useful.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the baseline can be an important component of neural activity that should be taken into account in order to find a compact information-rich neural code.
baseline correction can improve decoding performance in the presence of strong stimulus-evoked changes in firing rate.
baseline-corrected space by time non-negative matrix factorizations provide an efficient way to represent single-trial population spike trains in both the spatial and temporal dimensions.
